mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of lines are parallel?

options.A: Two lines that intersect at a right angle
options.B: Two lines that meet at a single point
options.C: Two lines that never meet and are the same distance apart everywhere
options.D: Two lines that cross each other forming an X

mcqs.answer: Two lines that never meet and are the same distance apart everywhere
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are defined as lines in the same plane that never intersect and stay at a constant distance from each other. Option C describes this property. Options A, B, and D describe intersecting lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: If two lines are parallel, what can be said about the distance between them at any two points on the lines?

options.A: The distance varies depending on where you measure
options.B: The distance is zero because they touch each other
options.C: The distance is the same at every point along the lines
options.D: The distance increases as you move away from the origin

mcqs.answer: The distance is the same at every point along the lines
mcqs.explanation: A defining property of parallel lines is that they stay equally separated; the perpendicular distance between them is constant. Options A, B, and D contradict this property.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: In a rectangle, which sides are parallel?

options.A: All four sides are parallel to each other
options.B: Only the opposite sides are parallel
options.C: No sides are parallel because a rectangle is a closed shape
options.D: Only the adjacent sides are parallel

mcqs.answer: Only the opposite sides are parallel
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle has two pairs of opposite sides that never meet and are equally spaced; these are parallel. Adjacent sides meet at right angles, so they are not parallel. Option B correctly identifies the parallel sides.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Which everyday object contains a pair of parallel lines?
mcqs.explanation: The long edges of a ruler run side by side without meeting, staying the same distance apart, which makes them parallel. Scissors, road intersections, and V‑shaped strings involve intersecting lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish parallel lines from intersecting lines
mcqs.question: Which picture shows intersecting lines rather than parallel lines?

options.A: Two straight lines drawn side by side that never meet
options.B: Two lines that cross each other forming an X
options.C: Two lines that are exactly on top of each other
options.D: Two lines that are drawn as a single straight line

mcqs.answer: Two lines that cross each other forming an X
mcqs.explanation: Intersecting lines meet at a point; option B describes this. Option A describes parallel lines, while C describes coincident lines (the same line) and D is just one line, not a pair.

mcqs.question: A student draws two lines on a notebook page. She measures the perpendicular distance between them at three different places and gets 2 cm each time. Which statement is true?

options.A: The lines are intersecting because the distance is measured
options.B: The lines are parallel because the distance stays the same
options.C: The lines are coincident because the distance is constant
options.D: The lines are curved, not straight

mcqs.answer: The lines are parallel because the distance stays the same
mcqs.explanation: A constant perpendicular distance between two straight lines indicates they are parallel. Intersecting lines would have varying distances, and coincident lines would have zero distance. The scenario confirms parallelism.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: A student claims that two parallel lines can get closer together if you look at them from a distance. Which response corrects this misconception?

options.A: The lines appear closer due to perspective, but mathematically their distance stays the same.
options.B: Parallel lines actually change their distance depending on the observer’s position.
options.C: If the lines are drawn on paper, they will physically move closer together.
options.D: Parallel lines are only a visual illusion; they do not have a real distance.

mcqs.answer: The lines appear closer due to perspective, but mathematically their distance stays the same.
mcqs.explanation: Parallelism is a geometric property independent of viewpoint. Perspective can make parallel lines look convergent, but their true perpendicular distance remains constant. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: In a regular hexagon, which of the following statements is true about its sides?

options.A: All six sides are parallel to each other
options.B: No sides are parallel because the shape is closed
options.C: Each side is parallel to the side that is opposite it

mcqs.answer: Each side is parallel to the side that is opposite it
mcqs.explanation: A regular hexagon has three pairs of opposite sides; each pair is parallel. Therefore, each side is parallel to the side directly opposite it. Options A and D are false because not all sides are parallel, and adjacent sides meet at vertices. Option B ignores the existence of opposite parallel sides.
